metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt Logs Limited Practice Session on Wednesday
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) logged a limited practice session on Wednesday due to a groin issue, per the team's official injury report. Croskey-Merritt recorded 2026 season lows in Week 4 in carries (nine), rushing yards (15), and rushing yards per attempt (1.7). He also had two receptions for 35 yards. Austin Ekeler, who recently signed back with the Commanders, outperformed Croskey-Merritt on the ground on fewer carries with 29 yards on four rushes (7.3 yards per carry). Ultimately, the Commanders were defeated 30-13 against the Indianapolis Colts in London in Week 4. Of note, fellow running back Rachaad White (shoulder) returned to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday after missing the game against the Colts in Week 4. Croskey-Merritt leads the Commanders with 56 rushing attempts for 157 yards and a touchdown, but he has been inefficient with an average of just 2.8 yards per carry. Croskey-Merritt's participation throughout the rest of the practice week will be telling, but he does not appear to be in danger of missing a Week 5 matchup with the New York Giants as of now.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: The young running back was left limited at the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday due to a groin injury that he's managing. He hasn't been very effective to start the year, so fantasy managers shouldn't be looking to start him this week even if he's fully healthy and available to play for the Commanders.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Limited with groin injury
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice session, Ralph Vacchiano of FoxSports.com
metadata.analysis: The Commanders have a lengthy injury report Wednesday, including their starting running back. Croskey-Merritt is dealing with a groin injury as the Commanders prepare to host the Giants, but he was at least able to get some work in. Fellow running back Rachaad White (shoulder) also logged a limited session.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt Busts in Fantasy Football for Third Game In A Row
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt had his third game with just single-digit PPR fantasy points in a row this season. He rushed nine times for 15 yards and caught two of his four targets for 35 yards. The Commanders suffered another injury at quarterback, as backup QB Marcus Mariota (knee) exited the game with a knee injury, leaving third-stringer and rookie Athan Kaliakmanis to serve as signal-caller. It resulted in Washington getting blown out by the opposing Indianapolis Colts, which isn't a huge surprise. WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) missed the game, so it's no surprise the Commanders couldn't move the ball, which likely contributed to Croskey-Merritt's inefficiency. He's now averaging just 3.0 yards per carry on the season. He looks like the undrafted free agent signing that he is, and it's hard to imagine he keeps his lead RB role for long, but Washington hasn't functioned competently as an organization from a personnel standpoint recently. The Giants will head to Washington to take on the Commanders in Week 5. JCM is a bench candidate -- even as the starter, his ceiling and floor are both extremely low.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt  quiet in Week 4 loss
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 15 yards on nine carries in the Commanders loss to the Colts. He caught 2-of-4 passes for 35 yards.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt and the entire Commanders' rushing attack struggled to get anything going against the Colts. With the current quarterback situation in Washington, Croskey-Merritt and the rest of the running backs could be asked to see more work in a Week 5 matchup with the Giants.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Held in check by Indy
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt carried the ball nine times for a season-low 15 yards and caught two of four targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
metadata.analysis: The Commanders' running game struggled to get anything going against an Indy front seven led by DeForest Buckner, especially once Marcus Mariota (knee) was replaced under center by seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis, but Croskey-Merritt was able to salvage his production to some extent with a 35-yard catch and run on a screen pass in the first quarter that helped set up a field goal. His 11 touches led the Washington backfield, while Austin Ekeler saw five in his season debut and rookie Kaytron Allen got three, but that division of labor came with Rachaad White (shoulder) on the shelf. Croskey-Merritt's ability to improve on his numbers could depend on whether Jayden Daniels (elbow) can return at quarterback for Washington in a Week 5 home game against the Giants.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt A Solid RB2 in Week 4 with Potential for Larger Role
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt handled a career-high 20 touches in Week 3's win over the Seattle Seahawks. Croskey-Merritt wasn't overly efficient on his touches, rushing for just 36 yards on 19 carries and adding one catch for seven yards, but the second-year back has seen steady volume in each game so far. Croskey-Merritt also had a 48-yard touchdown wiped out by an unfortunate illegal formation penalty. Now with Rachaad White (shoulder) ruled out for Week 4, Croskey-Merritt should maintain a high-volume role and potentially see more involvement as a receiver. It's an appealing Week 4 matchup against a Colts defense that is allowing the fourth most rushing yards per game (141.3) and tied for the second most rushing touchdowns (five) in the league through three games. In a game with one of the higher projected totals of the week, Croskey-Merritt projects as a solid RB2 for Week 4, ranking as RotoBaller's RB23 in PPR formats.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - In line for larger workload in London
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt has served as the Commanders' RB1 this season, but his backfield snap count for Week 4 against the Colts figures to be larger due to the absence of Rachaad White (shoulder).
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has logged 47 carries through three regular-season games, though he's turned that into only 142 yards (3.0 YPC) and a touchdown while playing less than 50 percent of the Commanders' offensive snaps in two different contests. White has mostly operated as the change-of-pace, pass-catching RB for Washington this season, so Croskey-Merritt figures to see an expanded role Sunday while the former is sidelined. Rookie Kaytron Allen and recently-signed Austin Ekeler also are in the mix for backfield work this weekend in London.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt bottled up in Week 3 win
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 19 times for 36 yards while also hauling in his only target for seven yards in the Commanders' 33-31 Week 3 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has struggled to make an impact out of the backfield of late, rushing for less than 50 yards in each of the last two games. The running back remains a risky lineup option in all formats ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Held in check by Seattle
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 19 times for 36 yards and caught his only target for seven yards in Sunday's 33-31 win over the Seahawks.
metadata.analysis: The second-year back couldn't get much going against the defending Super Bowl champs, with his longest run going for just nine yards, but the 20 touches did represent a season high in volume. Croskey-Merritt remains the top early-down option in the Commanders' backfield, and through three games he's gained 142 rushing yards and a TD on 47 carries. He could find more running room in a Week 4 home tilt against the Colts.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt A Risky Option in Week 3 Against Seattle
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was bottled up for only 48 yards on 13 touches in Week 2's loss to the Dallas Cowboys. And after leading Rachaad White in touches, 17 to nine, in Week 1, the two each saw 13 touches apiece in Week 2. White looked good and produced 83 total yards against Dallas and could see more work going forward. Among qualified rushers per NFL Pro, Croskey-Merritt's minus-25 rushing yards over expected ranks third worst. The second-year back will also be without the team's top QB in Jayden Daniels (elbow) as they face the vaunted Seattle Seahawks defense in Week 3, who are allowing 3.7 yards per carry so far this season, which is tied for seventh-best in the league. Croskey-Merritt projects as a low-end flex option in Week 3, coming in as RB40 in RotoBaller's Week 3 PPR rankings.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt's Weekly Fantasy Value Slipping Away
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt is trending down in fantasy football, largely due to his declining role on offense. Croskey-Merritt went from a 49% snap share and 16 carries in Week 1 to a 37% snap share and 12 carries in Week 2. Meanwhile, versatile teammate Rachaad White has stepped into a larger role and played more than half of the snaps last Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys. This could have been a result of game script, but more likely than not, it was fueled by Croskey-Merritt's inefficiency so far (3.8 YPC) and his lack of production in the receiving game. Going forward, Croskey-Merritt's fantasy value will continue to suffer from reduced volume, but he'll also take a further hit due to the state of the offense. The Commanders enter Week 3 without quarterback Jayden Daniels (elbow), which means that Marcus Mariota will take over the offense. It's hard to imagine Mariota keeping the Commanders in a competitive game against the Seahawks, and the resulting negative game script will have an unfavorable impact on Croskey-Merritt's role. He's a fringe RB3/flex in deep leagues against a strong Seattle defense.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Solid rushing day in loss
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt rushed 12 times for 43 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Commanders' 37-20 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt once again functioned as the lead back in the Commanders' ground attack, and he did reasonably well with his opportunities. Washington's offense took a significant hit when Jayden Daniels exited the game with an elbow injury on the final play of the first half, and Croskey-Merritt's opportunities on the ground were also somewhat capped in the second half with the Commanders trying to catch up. Croskey-Merritt should continue helming the run game in a Week 3 home matchup against the defending champion Seahawks next Sunday.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt sees 12 carries in Week 2 loss
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed for 43 yards on 12 carries and caught his lone target for five yards in the loss to Dallas Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt was out targeted by Rachaad White 6-to-1, but each tallied 43 yards on the ground. The Commanders' offense took a massive blow losing Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow, so the running game will likely be relied upon more heading into Week 3.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt Carries Flex Appeal Against Dallas
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt handled most of the rushing work in Week 1, carrying 16 times for 63 yards and a touchdown against Philadelphia. Rachaad White had seven carries and Kaytron Allen four, although the snaps were much closer, with Croskey-Merritt playing 34 and White 29. There are still reasons to be careful. Croskey-Merritt caught one pass for minus-seven yards, while White remained involved in the passing game, and Croskey-Merritt did not return after fumbling late in the fourth quarter. Allen handled the final drive. The matchup gives him a decent chance to stay involved, though. Dallas allowed 165 rushing yards to the Giants in Week 1, including 81 yards and a touchdown to Cam Skattebo. Croskey-Merritt is not a locked-in starter with Washington still using multiple backs, but the carry share and matchup make him a reasonable flex option for Week 2.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt Projects Favorably Against Cowboys
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt was productive as the team's lead back in the season opener against the Eagles, rushing for 63 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries. The second-year back handled 16 of 27 carries by Washington running backs and notably didn't see the field again after fumbling on the team's final drive. Rookie Kaytron Allen replaced Croskey-Merritt on the final drive, and after fumbling four times as a rookie, he could start to cede work to the rookie if it continues. However, Croskey-Merritt is still the team's most dynamic and explosive rusher and could be primed for a good day on the ground in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys. Dallas just allowed Cam Skattebo and the Giants to run for 165 yards on 4.5 yards per carry in Week 1, making Croskey-Merritt a solid flex option in Week 2.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt Takes Early Lead in Washington Backfield
metadata.description: Washington Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt didn't take over the backfield in Week 1, but the rushing split was hard to miss. He carried 16 times for 63 yards and a touchdown against Philadelphia. Rachaad White had seven carries, while rookie Kaytron Allen had four. The snaps were much closer, with Croskey-Merritt at 49% and White at 41%, so White isn't disappearing from this offense. He also caught both of his targets, while Croskey-Merritt's only reception went for minus-seven yards. Still, Washington gave Croskey-Merritt 16 of its 27 running back carries, and he punched in a one-yard touchdown late in the first half. He did put the ball on the ground once, though the Commanders recovered it. Croskey-Merritt was already listed first on the depth chart before the opener. The game told us more than the depth chart did. For now, he looks like the back Washington wants handling most of the rushing work.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt reaches end zone in Week 1 loss
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt carried the ball 16 times for 63 yards and one touchdown while also catching his only target for a loss of seven yards in the Commanders' 24-22 Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt made the most of his opportunities out of the backfield, accounting for 50% of the carries for the Commanders in Week 1. The running back seems poised to receive as much volume as he can handle as the primary option out of the backfield to begin the season for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 2 divisional matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Gets into end zone in Week 1 win
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt rushed 16 times for 63 yards and a touchdown while catching his only target for a seven-yard loss in a defeat to the Eagles on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt scored Washington's only touchdown of the first half when he plunged into the end zone for a one-yard score late in the second quarter. However, he averaged just 3.9 yards per carry and also lost a fumble, though the Commanders were able to recover. Croskey-Merritt served as Washington's clear No. 1 back in terms of totes, with Rachaad White (seven carries for 22 yards) and Kaytron Allen (four carries for 16 yards) working behind him, though White's pass-catching role did garner him 27 offensive snaps to Croskey-Merritt's 33. The Commanders will take on Dallas in a Week 2 clash next Sunday.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - No designation for Week 1
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt had his practice reps restricted during the entirety of Week 1 prep due to a lower-body injury that stems back to an Aug. 22 practice. Despite those listed limitations, he'll be available to the Commanders backfield this weekend, likely in some sort of timeshare with Rachaad White.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1
metadata.description: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Week 1 for the Washington Commanders against the Philadelphia Eagles according to Ian Rapoport.

metadata.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt - Will play in Week 1
metadata.description: Croskey-Merritt (groin) will play in Sunday's game against the Eagles, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Croskey-Merritt was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but will apparently be fine for the season opener. He's got a tough matchup on the road in Philadelphia, and he'll will be sharing snaps with Rachaad White in some fashion, regardless of health/durability considerations.
